messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call — sustained tail latency on streaming API (p95 and p99 breach). Alert: streaming.tail.latency > 300ms for 5m. Thread TS 1752468100

maya: I see alerts too. p95 ~560ms, p99 spiking to ~2.4s on /v1/stream/chat (us-east shared pool). Multiple customers reporting stalls.

liam: which pool and hosts? any recent deploys?

ops-bot: active_pool=shared-gpu-us-east-2, hosts impacted: host-a23, host-a27. No deploys in last 30m. GPU util steady ~85-95%. nvme avg latency climbing (host-a23=62ms, host-a27=70ms).

emic: running quick `iotop` and `pss`. I/O shows heavy writeback from container tenant `orch-run` on host-a27. Many small random writes, sustained 700MB/s.

maya: `orch-run` — is that a customer batch job? who owns it?

emic: owner tag: tenant=orch-run (internal beta customer), repo=orch-batch, reason=checkpointing and flush operations.

liam: confirm impact: other tenants on same host experiencing streaming stalls because writeback saturates NVMe and blocks grpc writes. Also seeing increased kv-cache evictions correlated with spike.

maya: severity: Sev-2 (SLOs degraded, multiple customers). Notify CS to warn customers of degraded streaming. @cs-notify please broadcast to affected list.

cs-notify: notified affected customers with advisory: "We are investigating elevated streaming latency; mitigation in progress."

emic: quick mitigation options: 1) lower blkio.weight for orch-run container, 2) pause checkpointing via signal if supported, 3) live-migrate container to dedicated pool.

liam: try soft throttle first. Do blkio weight to 150 (default 1000). Command:
```
# apply blkio weight
cgset -r blkio.weight=/containers/tenant-orch-run 150
```

ops-bot: applied blkio.weight=150 on host-a27 at 16:12 UTC. Monitoring...

emic: nvme_avg_lat on host-a27 dropped to ~22ms within 45s. p95 trending down to ~240ms, p99 ~780ms. Still some intermittent spikes.

maya: Good. But p99 still high; might be cache thrash. Let's also enable kv-cache protective mode: reduce cache insert rate for low-priority routes.

liam: doing that now. `kvcachectl set policy low_priority_inserts=false`

ops-bot: KV cache insert rate reduced. Evictions decreasing.

emic: spikes still at p99 (~1.1s) — probably due to open streaming connections queued while writeback drains. Consider live-evac of orch-run to dedicated-surge-1.

maya: agree. Stage migration of a single replica first to minimize churn. Prepare dedicated slot and transfer model artifacts.

liam: staging migration, creating dedicated allocation dedicated-surge-1, copying checkpoints. Note: snapshot transfer will hit network; watch nvme/nic on both ends.

ops-bot: migration started at 16:19 UTC. Snapshotting container fs -> 40%

emic: migrating one replica now. Redirecting small fraction of traffic to new instance for canary.

ops-bot: canary replica is up at 16:24 UTC on dedicated-surge-1. Traffic shifted 30% for validation. No errors observed. nvme on host-a27 drops to 10ms. p95 120ms, p99 380ms.

maya: good. ramp to 100% traffic to new pool for orch-run.

liam: ramp complete at 16:27 UTC. host-a27 nvme latency normal. streaming p95 stable ~110ms, p99 ~250ms and falling.

maya: mitigation successful. Customer impact window: 16:0616:27 UTC (approx). Brief elevated latency and sporadic stalls; no sustained downtime. CS notified.

emic: root-cause hypothesis: orch-run's checkpoint flush pattern caused sustained small random NVMe writes that overwhelmed the device's IO scheduler under cgroup mapping. This caused streaming RPCs to wait on disk writeback. Contributing factor: lack of writeback shaping per-tenant for bursty checkpoint workloads.

liam: follow-ups: 1) implement auto-detect rule for host nvme_avg_lat > 40ms + kv_cache_evictions > baseline -> auto-throttle suspects, 2) add tenant I/O admission policy to cap checkpoint write bursts, 3) expand runbook with forced-evacuate steps and canary migration checklist.

maya: owners: detection rule -> liam, tenant admission policy -> emic, runbook update -> maya. I'll create tasks and tag owners.

ops-bot: created task INS-2026 for runbook updates, assigned to maya. INS-2027 for detection rule to liam. INS-2028 for tenant I/O policy to emic.

cs-notify: will coordinate customer-facing post-incident summary once postmortem draft is ready.

maya: closing incident to monitoring at 16:36 UTC. Please reopen if we see regressions. :white_check_mark:
